title: Heat and Thermodynamics
seo_title: Physics 2: Heat and Thermodynamics Worksheets (Strengthened SHS)
standard_text: Heat in systems: temperature and heat, specific heat capacity, phase changes and latent heat, thermal expansion and heat transfer; thermodynamic processes and the zeroth, first and second laws of thermodynamics; heat engines. (summary of the Strengthened Senior High School curriculum, Physics 2, Quarter 4)
meta_desc: Free Physics 2 worksheets (Strengthened SHS curriculum, Quarter 4): temperature and heat, specific heat, latent heat, thermal expansion, the laws of thermodynamics and heat engines. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

Temperature measures the average kinetic energy of particles; heat is energy transferred because of a temperature difference. Q = mcΔT gives the heat needed to change temperature; Q = mL gives the heat for a change of phase. Most materials expand when heated.

The zeroth law defines thermal equilibrium; the first law (ΔU = Q − W) is conservation of energy; the second law says heat flows naturally from hot to cold and no heat engine can be 100% efficient. Efficiency = work out ÷ heat in.

Example

Heat to warm 2 kg of water by 10 °C (c = 4,186 J/kg·°C)?

Q = mcΔT

Answer: 83,720 J

Example

A gas absorbs 500 J and does 200 J of work. ΔU?

Q − W

Answer: 300 J

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up heat and temperature.
  • Forgetting that the temperature stays constant during a phase change.
  • Thinking a heat engine can turn all heat into work.
